correctness.rationale: The harmonic orthonormal monomial basis is indexed by positive/negative integers; direct projection T_(z^N) and N-fold one-step shift (T_z)^N agree outside e_-j (1<=j<N). On that finite cross-zero band the amplitudes differ by h_N/sqrt(h_j h_(N-j))-sqrt(h_j h_(N-j)). Beta moment h_j=E[X^j], X~Beta(1,a), has strictly positive covariance h_N-h_j h_(N-j). The ratio h_(k+1)/h_k=(k+1)/(k+a+1) is strictly increasing, so central h_j h_(N-j) is minimal and the coefficient maximal. Outgoing modes are positive indices and cannot feed D_N a second time, giving D_N^2=0. Bulk gamma-ratio h_j~Gamma(a+1)j^(-a), uniformly j/N away from 0,1, yields the t(1-t) profile. Bounded finite-rank coefficients control endpoint mass; beta integral and ordered central window yield all fixed-p Schatten and quantile claims. The normalization alpha>-1, N>=2, 0<p<infinity and endpoint p limits were checked. Independent rational coefficient, central symmetry and bulk calculations corroborate, not prove, infinite N.

originality.rationale: The older finite-rank generalized two-factor harmonic Bergman Toeplitz calculations explain the finite-support defect mechanism; rank alone is not new. Primary Dong–Zhou (2014) treats quasihomogeneous TWO-FACTOR commutators/semicommutators and their canonical ranges, not growing N-fold monomial powers with nondegenerate empirical singular distribution, every beta weight and all fixed Schatten exponents. Huang–Wang–Zhao 2026 concerns spectra of individual polynomial Toeplitz operators, not this difference. No inspected statement yields the beta bulk/quantile theorem; a compressed bilateral-shift formulation might nevertheless predate it.

value.rationale: The failure of multiplicativity of harmonic Bergman compression is a canonical operator-theoretic obstruction. Its rank grows with N; the new exactly normalized beta-profile distribution, central spectral edge and all Schatten exponents give natural complete asymptotic invariants rather than isolated finite coefficients. These facts can calibrate operator-norm approximation and nonmultiplicative functional calculus; they are not merely rank-one arithmetic.
